findings.description: The workflow injects inputs.authorization_sha256 || repository HARNESS_RELEASE_AUTHORIZATION_SHA256 on every event, including trusted main pushes. buildCiPlan treats any nonempty injected checksum as mandatory and throws on an old checksum, even when the committed source-bound authorization is valid. A retained prior-release repository variable therefore makes the next main push fail during planning. Restrict repository-variable fallback to PR approval; explicit manual checksums must still fail closed when invalid, while trusted main validates its committed source-bound authorization without stale repository state. Cover actual buildCiPlan and workflow event selection, not only selectCiPlan.

readAccount publishes accountCatalogSnapshot before the dedicated probe cleanup is confirmed, and always deletes the probe from catalogProcesses even when probe.close rejects. Unlike probeDefaults it neither marks runtime activity unknown nor emits fatal. Subsequent model/list can use that pre-cleanup cache and the service continues admitting work; whole-service close no longer includes the uncertain probe. Its generation check also happens before cleanup, so account/updated or service.close during the cleanup await allows stale account success to reach the caller. Publish cache/result only after confirmed cleanup plus generation and closed checks; retain failed cleanup authority and fail the epoch consistently instead of silently discarding it. Preserve singleflight and bounded retry behavior.

The operational documentation says resource/skill/read permits only the registered project and fixed global roots. The implemented M240 contract additionally permits precise ancestor .agents/skills directories up to the nearest actual non-symlink Git worktree root. The restrictive implementation is correct and covered, but the documented exhaustive allowlist is outdated and can mislead an operator investigating why an ancestor skill is readable.
Deleted selected provider falls back to the default while retaining another provider catalog draft
